searchText: Hey guys, just got back from vacation I wouldn't recommend rolling out the 5.1 upgrade in parallel with 5.0 We should consider that only if medalla is truly the last testnet before mainnet launches The 5.1 changes are not that big, but they are incompatible > We should consider that only if medalla is truly the last testnet before mainnet launches Having at least one other testnet in parallel to retest genesis and strive for better client diversity has been discussed. (As a side note, Medalla is currently under a lot strain.) I feel slightly bad for delaying the 5.1 spec so much because we're now at the point where mainnet is very much imminent and we won't have 2 months of cross client testnet run with the final packet encoding how many days would you estimate it take to upgrade a discv5 lib to 5.1? That said, the protocol semantics are pretty well tested at this point and 5.1 is just a format change It took me about two days to implement in go > mainnet is very much imminent and we won't have 2 months of cross client testnet run with the final packet encoding This is just my gut feel, but there's probably significantly more than 2 months from today before mainnet. Piper can say how long it took him Oh, cool, I was under the impression that it would launch earlier than that This is good news for me then! Piper has already made test vectors for 5.1, I'll get those integrated ASAP > This is good news for me then! Yay 🙂 In terms of community expectations the hard deadline is December 31, 2020. We may have to make the most of every day. OK, nice. Again, sorry for the huge delay on the 5.1 spec, but y'all know what's up in the world right now and I just couldn't get it done quicker. [probably not the best place to discuss dates.] depending on how medalla falls in the next few days, we may or may not do another large public testnet As for other items. There are a number of parallel nets to be built and tested for stress testing, practicing genesis, etc <-- on all of those we could test 5.1 And for mainnet, there will be a "genesis delay" of somewhere between 4 and 7 days. If any issues in discovery happened on the early end of that, we could go in and debug before the date. Probably not optimal to have mainnet not have the same discovery version as a "final" testnet, but I also don't particularly want to do an in flight discovery upgrade if we can avoid it Understood. In other news: the topic index simulation project is going very well. We now have an implementation of most of the protocol in PeerSim, a discrete event simulator written in Java. The existing impl. could not be reused because these kinds of simulators want you to use their API for scheduling events such as message sends and timers. Our baseline result by now is that the DHT is indeed converging, but we had already kind of confirmed that with the eth2 testnets I guess. The team is currently implementing a couple different algorithms for the topic index and then we'll be able to run those and get network-wide event traces from the simulation. > DHT is indeed converging can you define converging here? Someone in the team is also working on a loader for the DHT crawler JSON dump format that we produce using go-ethereum. By converging, I mean that the nodes form a healthy network without islands using the basic, Kademlia-like DHT protocol that we have. got it > a couple different algorithms are these different from that previously specified? The algo in the spec doesn't really work, which is why we're not using it (in eth2). They had a couple ideas for improving it, they're in the spec issue tracker. We're looking to implement those ideas, basically I'm excited about it, not just for eth2, but also because figuring out decentralized service discovery would be a genuine improvement for 'future internet' purposes.
